open_questions: Why transits 51 and -51 show 1440 ppm vs -160 ppm outlier depths despite flat shape and on-target location — spot crossings on spotted VARIABLE star?
Origin of marginal secondary at phase ~0.265 and long-term depth scatter with chi2 77.58 dof 6 — requires ground-based transit photometry at predicted 13.9 d to verify achromatic, consistent depth.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 13.9-day, 3.5-hour, flat-bottom dip of about 680 ppm repeating six to seven times on the target K dwarf, implying a ~2.3 Earth-radius planet. One transit disappeared and another was twice as deep, causing odd-even and sector depth differences, but there is no star nearby that can mimic the signal and no clear binary secondary. The depth scatter likely comes from spot activity on this variable star and can be tested with follow-up photometry.

reasons.why: Flat-bottom transit with duration.ratio 0.9267 and central_h 3.776 vs observed_h 3.5 favours planet over V-shaped binary or grazing EB.
Planet-sized 2.3 Rearth from undiluted_depth_ppm 680.2, well below stellar eclipse regime.
No star within one TESS pixel could cause the dip; closest that could is 49.4 arcsec needing 0.4031 eclipse, and centroid.verdict inconclusive not off-target.

Depth changes including -138 ppm in sector 15, but transit_depths shows the same instability on individual transits (p_consistent 1.1275480262352617e-14) with a -160 ppm non-detection and 1440 ppm deep event, so instability is epoch-to-epoch on_target, not a calibration offset or different aperture NEB blend.
reasons.value: changes_within_a_source with p_constant_all 4.926666284535527e-07 and SPOC p_constant 6.108383524068993e-07

reasons.why: Odd/even difference at 3.5 sigma with depth_ratio 2.3 and depth_difference 500.3 ppm is below 4 sigma and strongly driven by the same outlier transit (sector 15 non-detection) that drives transit_depths scatter; no positive secondary (snr_at_half -3.484).

Secondary at phase 0.2655 with depth_ppm 142.4 is at the 5 sigma threshold and offset (secondary_phase_offset 0.2345) with depth_over_dip 0.2147, against best_brightening_snr 6.724; ratio_to_depth 0.1346 and xgboost planet_rank 0.49 suggest it is not a stellar companion signal.
